To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quasi-steady-state approximation can be used to accurately predict the hitting probability and the conditional MFPT of the random search for a hidden absorptive target by a motor-based particle moving along a one-dimensional track, and that the quasi-stey state approximation can be used as a tool for analyzing the biophysical mechanisms underlying motor transport and synaptic targeting in neurons.
we developed a novel quasi-steady-state reduction of a molecular motor-based model of intermittent directed search that yields results in agreement with Monte Carlo simulation of the full model.

a quasi-steadystate reduction of a linear master equation describing a molecular motor model of directed intermittent search for synaptic targets yields a scalar FP equation with a target absorption term that can be used to compute the hitting probability and MFPT in terms of effective parameters V, D, λ, which can be determined from the biophysical parameters of a multiple motor model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a quasi-stead state reduction of a molecular motor-based model of directed intermittent search.
the development of a quasi-stead state reduction of a master equation model of motor-based transport and its application to the problem of directed search for a synaptic target.
the analysis of stochastic models of motor-driven transport in neurons, and the development of efficient computational methods for the analysis of such models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quasi-steady-state reduction provides an accurate approximation for the probability distribution function of the position of the particle and the hitting probability, but the conditional mean first passage times are only accurate for the case where the target is far from the particle injection point.
the quasi-steady reduction is very useful in analyzing complex molecular motor-based models of directed search.

the quasi-steady-state reduction of the master equation is very powerful in providing a simple analytical description of the dynamics of the motor-based models of the directed intermittent search, in which the effective drift velocity, diffusivity, and target absorption are determined by the parameters of the underlying biophysical model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our quasi-stedy state reduction provides a powerful method for the analysis of directed intermittent search, and that our results can be used to guide the design of molecular motors for targeted cargo delivery.

we have developed a general method for analyzing a large class of stochastic models that are based on the dynamics of molecular motors, which is applicable to the analysis of a wide range of biological problems.
our quasi-stated reduction is a powerful tool for analyzing the directed intermittent search of a particle driven by a molecular motor on a filament track.
The main takeaway from our work is that
quasi-steady states can provide a simple and effective framework for the analysis of molecular motor-based directed intermittent search.
quasi-steady-state reductions can provide an efficient way of studying the directed search dynamics in molecular motor models of vesicle transport.

the quasi-steady-state reduction of a master equation describing directed intermittent search by a molecular motor-driven particle is an efficient way to compute the probability that the hidden target is found (hitting probability), and the corresponding mean first passage time.
